problem: "often once per engine revolution or twice per cycle" is presented as two alternatives, but on a four-stroke engine they are the same thing (two revolutions per cycle, one pulse per revolution = two pulses per cycle). A student reads it as two different possible rates and gets confused.
fix: Write: "The injector fires at a fixed rate tied to engine speed — typically once per engine revolution, which is twice per four-stroke cycle. Only the pulse width changes."

problem: "a cam or crank sensor that identifies the cylinder" — a crank sensor alone gives speed and piston position but cannot tell which cylinder is on its compression stroke, so it cannot identify the cylinder. This also sits badly with the exam trap that says sequential needs cylinder identification, not just crank speed.
fix: Write: "Sequential gives the best fuel control and cold-start behaviour but needs a camshaft (cylinder-identification) sensor, because a crank sensor alone gives speed and position but not the stroke phase."

problem: "Sensors turn physical quantities into voltages" contradicts the coolant sensor line, which says the sensor is a thermistor, i.e. it changes resistance, not voltage.
fix: Write: "Sensors turn physical quantities into electrical signals: some give a voltage directly (hot-wire air flow, oxygen cell), others change resistance and the ECU converts that to a voltage (coolant thermistor, potentiometer throttle sensor)."
